subject: general
question: The atomic number of an atom is equal to the:

options.text: total number of protons present in the nucleus of an atom
sum of the number of electrons and that of neutrons
half of the number of electrons present in the nucleus of an atom
sum of the number of protons and that of neutrons

solution:
The correct answer is __**total number of protons present in the nucleus of an atom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The atomic number of an atom is defined as the number of protons present in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• It is unique for each element and determines the identity of the element.
 
• The atomic number is denoted by the symbol 'Z'.
 
• In a neutral atom, the number of electrons is equal to the number of protons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protons:**

 
 
• Protons are positively charged particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of protons in the nucleus determines the atomic number and the identity of the element.
 
• Protons have a relative charge of +1 and a relative mass of 1 atomic mass unit (amu).
 
 
 
• **Neutrons:**
 
 
• Neutrons are neutral particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• They have no electrical charge but contribute to the atomic mass of an atom.
 
• The number of neutrons in an atom can vary, resulting in different isotopes of an element.
 
 
 
• **Electrons:**
 
 
• Electrons are negatively charged particles that orbit the nucleus of an atom in various energy levels.
 
• In a neutral atom, the number of electrons is equal to the number of protons.
 
• Electrons have a relative charge of -1 and a very small relative mass (approximately 1/1836 of a proton).
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
 
• This difference in neutron number results in different atomic masses for the isotopes.
 
• For example, Carbon-12 and Carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon with 6 protons but 6 and 8 neutrons respectively.
